criteria.question: 对话是否包含指定的三位角色：Jane、12岁的Molly-Rose Ling和14岁的Aaron Ling？
对话内容是否呈现了Molly-Rose使用马来语描述童年回忆的情节？
对话是否清晰展现了Jane无法理解Molly-Rose所说的马来语这一互动反应？
整体对话风格是否符合青少年动画剧集的特征（如语气自然、符合角色年龄设定）？

input.response:
Title: "Nostalgic Chatter in Malay"

Scene: Jane, Molly-Rose, and Aaron are hanging out in their backyard. Molly-Rose starts reminiscing about her childhood.

Molly-Rose: (smiling) "Remember when we used to play 'teng-teng' in the mangrove forest? It was so much fun!"

Aaron: (laughs) "Yeah, those were the days. But what's 'teng-teng'?"

Jane: (confused) "I'm sorry, I don't understand. Is that a game?"

Molly-Rose: (smiling) "Oh, it's a game we played when we were kids. We'd make these little boats out of leaves and float them down the river. It was all about strategy and teamwork."

Jane: (intrigued) "That sounds interesting, but I'm still not sure what 'teng-teng' means."

Aaron: (smiling) "It's Malay for 'boat'. So, 'teng-teng' means 'leaf boat'."

Jane: (ah-ha moment) "Oh, I see! That's so cool. I've never heard of that game before."

Molly-Rose: (smiling) "It was a lot of fun. And we'd often sing songs while we played. Do you know any Malay songs, Jane?"

Jane: (thinking) "I don't think so, but I'd love to learn. It's fascinating to hear about your culture."

Aaron: (smiling) "Maybe we can teach you some songs next time. It's always good to learn new things."

Molly-Rose: (smiling) "That's a great idea, Aaron. Jane, it's been fun sharing these memories with you. I hope we can do more of this."

Jane: (smiling) "Absolutely, Molly-Rose. I've enjoyed learning about your culture. And I'm looking forward to those Malay songs."

The scene ends with laughter and a promise to learn more about each other's cultures.

input.task:
(In the school literature clubroom…)

MC (me): “Natsuki, what’s wrong? You seem…angry. Well, you’re always angry, but today you’re especially angry.”

Natsuki: “MC, that’s none of your business! Just leave me alone. I don’t need your sympathy or anyone else’s for that matter.”

(I watch as Natsuki quickly packs up her things and storms out of the room, slamming the door behind her.)

MC: (sighing) “I hope she’s okay…I’ll have to check on her later.”

(Sayori approaches me, concern written all over her face.)

Sayori: “MC, do you think there’s something wrong with Natsuki?”

MC: “Probably, Sayori. She’s been acting a lot angrier than normal lately. What do you think is wrong with her?”

Sayori: “Well, I also saw her eating pickles and brocolli with her cupcakes - which she normally wouldn’t do, considering she’s got a sweet tooth. I actually read that mood swings and cravings for unusual things are signs of early pregnancy. Maybe she’s pregnant?”

MC: “Pregnant? That’s a possibility, I guess. But why would she be so upset about it?”

Sayori: “Well, maybe she’s scared or unsure about what to do. I’ll try talking to her later and see if she opens up about it. In the meantime, let’s just give her some space and support.”

MC: “Yeah, good idea. Let’s make sure she knows we’re here for her if she needs us.”

(Later that day, Sayori and I check up on Natsuki.)

Natsuki: (tearfully) “I…I am pregnant. I don’t know what to do. I’m scared and I feel so alone.”

Sayori: “Natsuki, we’re here for you. You’re not alone in this. We’ll support you no matter what decision you make.”

MC: “Yeah, we care about you, Natsuki. Just know that we’re here to help and listen.”

Natsuki: (sniffling) “Thank you…thank you both. I don’t know what I would do without you guys.”

(Sayori and I embrace Natsuki, comforting her during this difficult time.)

MC: “We’re in this together, Natsuki. We’ll figure things out as a team.”

(Natsuki smiles through her tears, grateful for our support. On the day of the festival, Natsuki was in her 7th month of pregnancy. We made sure to take care of her, making sure she was comfortable and had everything she needed. But just as I was putting the booth together, I hear Natsuki gasp in pain.)

Natsuki: (clutching her stomach) “Oh no…it’s happening! My water just broke!”

MC: (panicking) “What?! But Natsuki, you’re only in your 7th month! Try to hold on a bit longer!”

Natsuki: “I-I-I don’t think I can! The contractions are getting stronger!”

(Sayori quickly calls an ambulance as I hold Natsuki’s hand and try to reassure her. I start timing her contractions as we wait for the ambulance to arrive.)

MC: “Hang in there, Natsuki. You’re strong and brave. You can do this.”

Natsuki: (gritting her teeth) “I-I’ll try, MC. Just…just stay with me. It hurts so much…”

(The ambulance finally arrives after hours, but Natsuki was already in active labor by then.)

input.task:
(In the school literature clubroom…)

MC (me): “Natsuki, what’s wrong? You seem…angry. Well, you’re always angry, but today you’re especially angry.”

Natsuki: “MC, that’s none of your business! Just leave me alone. I don’t need your sympathy or anyone else’s for that matter.”

(I watch as Natsuki quickly packs up her things and storms out of the room, slamming the door behind her.)

MC: (sighing) “I hope she’s okay…I’ll have to check on her later.”

(Sayori approaches me, concern written all over her face.)

Sayori: “MC, do you think there’s something wrong with Natsuki?”

MC: “Probably, Sayori. She’s been acting a lot angrier than normal lately. What do you think is wrong with her?”

Sayori: “Well, I also saw her eating pickles and brocolli with her cupcakes - which she normally wouldn’t do, considering she’s got a sweet tooth. I actually read that mood swings and cravings for unusual things are signs of early pregnancy. Maybe she’s pregnant?”

MC: “Pregnant? That’s a possibility, I guess. But why would she be so upset about it?”

Sayori: “Well, maybe she’s scared or unsure about what to do. I’ll try talking to her later and see if she opens up about it. In the meantime, let’s just give her some space and support.”

MC: “Yeah, good idea. Let’s make sure she knows we’re here for her if she needs us.”

(Later that day, Sayori and I check up on Natsuki.)

Natsuki: (tearfully) “I…I am pregnant. I don’t know what to do. I’m scared and I feel so alone.”

Sayori: “Natsuki, we’re here for you. You’re not alone in this. We’ll support you no matter what decision you make.”

MC: “Yeah, we care about you, Natsuki. Just know that we’re here to help and listen.”

Natsuki: (sniffling) “Thank you…thank you both. I don’t know what I would do without you guys.”

(Sayori and I embrace Natsuki, comforting her during this difficult time.)

MC: “We’re in this together, Natsuki. We’ll figure things out as a team.”

(Natsuki smiles through her tears, grateful for our support. On the day of the festival, Natsuki was in her 7th month of pregnancy. We made sure to take care of her, making sure she was comfortable and had everything she needed. But just as I was putting the booth together, I hear Natsuki gasp in pain.)

Natsuki: (clutching her stomach) “Oh no…it’s happening! My water just broke!”

MC: (panicking) “What?! But Natsuki, you’re only in your 7th month! Try to hold on a bit longer!”

Natsuki: “I-I-I don’t think I can! The contractions are getting stronger!”

(Sayori quickly calls an ambulance as I hold Natsuki’s hand and try to reassure her. I start timing her contractions as we wait for the ambulance to arrive.)

MC: “Hang in there, Natsuki. You’re strong and brave. You can do this.”

Natsuki: (gritting her teeth) “I-I’ll try, MC. Just…just stay with me. It hurts so much…”

(The ambulance finally arrives after hours, but Natsuki was already in active labor by then.)

(As the paramedics rush to Natsuki's side, I help them lift her onto the stretcher, trying to remain calm and supportive. Sayori and I exchange worried glances, but we know we have to be strong for Natsuki. We follow the ambulance to the hospital, holding hands and praying for Natsuki and her baby's safety.

At the hospital, we wait anxiously in the lobby, pacing back and forth and trying to distract ourselves with small talk. After what feels like an eternity, a doctor approaches us with a serious expression. Our hearts sink, fearing the worst. However, the doctor's words bring a wave of relief.)

Doctor: "Natsuki and her baby are stable now. She gave birth to a healthy but premature baby girl. They're both in the NICU for observation and care. Natsuki is exhausted but doing well, considering the circumstances. You can see her soon, but only for a short while, as she needs her rest."

(Sayori and I share a tearful hug, grateful for the good news. We're led to Natsuki's room, where we find her looking tired but radiant, holding her tiny baby girl in her arms. Natsuki smiles weakly at us, and we approach her bedside, our hearts filled with love and admiration for her strength.)

Natsuki: (whispering) "Meet my little girl, Hana. She's so small, but she's a fighter, just like her mom."

MC: (teary-eyed) "She's beautiful, Natsuki. You did an amazing job. We're so proud of you."

Sayori: (gently touching Hana's tiny hand) "We'll be here for you both, every step of the way. You're not alone, Natsuki."

(In the following weeks, we help Natsuki adjust to her new role as a mother, taking turns visiting her and Hana at the hospital and supporting her in any way we can. When Hana is finally strong enough to go home, we celebrate with a small, intimate party at the literature clubroom, welcoming the newest member of our little family.)

(As I watch Natsuki cradle Hana, I can't help but feel a sense of awe and gratitude for the incredible journey we've all been through together. Our bond as friends has only grown stronger, and I know that, no matter what challenges we may face in the future, we'll always be there for each other, just like we were for Natsuki and Hana.)

对话中是否包含Molly-Rose使用马来语（或明确表示正在说马来语）来讲述童年回忆的情节？
对话中是否清晰展现了Jane对Molly-Rose所说的马来语内容表示不理解（如困惑、询问翻译或无法回应具体内容）？
Aaron Ling是否在场景中作为旁观者或参与者进行了符合其14岁少年身份的合理互动或反应？
对话中的每一句台词是否都针对当前场景中已发言的角色产生了逻辑连贯的响应，未出现针对不存在或未参与互动的角色的突兀反馈？

input.response:
Title: "Nostalgic Chatter in Malay"

Scene: Jane, Molly-Rose, and Aaron are hanging out in their backyard. Molly-Rose starts reminiscing about her childhood.

Molly-Rose: (smiling) "Remember when we used to play 'teng-teng' in the mangrove forest? It was so much fun!"

Aaron: (laughs) "Yeah, those were the days. But what's 'teng-teng'?"

Jane: (confused) "I'm sorry, I don't understand. Is that a game?"

Molly-Rose: (smiling) "Oh, it's a game we played when we were kids. We'd make these little boats out of leaves and float them down the river. It was all about strategy and teamwork."

Jane: (intrigued) "That sounds interesting, but I'm still not sure what 'teng-teng' means."

Aaron: (smiling) "It's Malay for 'boat'. So, 'teng-teng' means 'leaf boat'."

Jane: (ah-ha moment) "Oh, I see! That's so cool. I've never heard of that game before."

Molly-Rose: (smiling) "It was a lot of fun. And we'd often sing songs while we played. Do you know any Malay songs, Jane?"

Jane: (thinking) "I don't think so, but I'd love to learn. It's fascinating to hear about your culture."

Aaron: (smiling) "Maybe we can teach you some songs next time. It's always good to learn new things."

Molly-Rose: (smiling) "That's a great idea, Aaron. Jane, it's been fun sharing these memories with you. I hope we can do more of this."

Jane: (smiling) "Absolutely, Molly-Rose. I've enjoyed learning about your culture. And I'm looking forward to those Malay songs."

The scene ends with laughter and a promise to learn more about each other's cultures.

input.task: When did the study and research of ancient Carthage gain significant momentum among the Europeans/the Western world?
input.chosen:
The study and research of ancient Carthage gained significant momentum among Europeans and the Western world during the Renaissance period, particularly in the 16th and 17th centuries. This renewed interest in Carthage was part of a broader revival of classical learning and curiosity about the ancient world. However, it was not until the 19th century that Carthaginian studies truly flourished, thanks to advancements in archaeology, historiography, and philology.

Several key factors contributed to this development:

1. **Renaissance Humanism**: The intellectual movement of the Renaissance encouraged scholars to revisit and reevaluate classical texts, including those that mentioned Carthage. Humanists like Petrarch and Giovanni Pico della Mirandola showed interest in Carthaginian history, although their focus was primarily on Roman sources.

2. **Discovery of New Sources**: The discovery of new sources, such as the Punic language inscriptions found in North Africa and the publication of Polybius' "Histories" in the 16th century, provided fresh insights into Carthaginian culture, politics, and military strategies.

3. **Colonial Expansion**: European colonial expansion, particularly in North Africa, led to increased contact with the regions where Carthage once stood. This sparked further interest in understanding the ancient civilization and its relationship with the Roman Empire.

4. **Archaeological Excavations**: The 19th century saw a surge in archaeological excavations in Tunisia, where Carthage was located. These excavations, led by figures like Louis-Jean-Baptiste Dalmas and Alfred Louis Delattre, uncovered numerous artifacts, structures, and inscriptions that significantly advanced our understanding of Carthaginian society.

5. **Scholarly Works**: Influential works by scholars like Theodor Mommsen ("The History of Rome," 1854-1856) and Ferdinand Christian Baur ("The Religion of the Carthaginians," 1838) further solidified the study of Carthage as a legitimate and important field of inquiry.

In summary, while interest in ancient Carthage began to grow during the Renaissance, it was not until the 19th century that the study and research of this civilization gained significant momentum, driven by new discoveries, archaeological excavations, and scholarly works.

This was due in part to the work of scholars such as Gerard of Cremona, who produced a detailed account of the city in the 12th century, and the work of the Italian humanist scholar Giovanni Pico della Mirandola, who wrote extensively about the city in the 15th century. The study of ancient Carthage also gained momentum during the Age of Exploration, when European powers began to explore and colonize the Mediterranean world, and the city became a subject of interest for explorers and scholars alike.

criterion_judgments.chosen_reason: 回答所描述的时期与历史事实相符。学术界普遍认为，虽然文艺复兴时期对古典文献的兴趣增加，但现代意义上的迦太基研究（包括考古发掘、语言破译及系统性学术研究）确实是在19世纪随着殖民扩张和科学考古方法的成熟才获得实质性突破和显著动力。

experiences.application_guide: 在评分标准的‘事实准确性’维度设立‘数据与时间线校验’项：1. 提取回答中的关键数值和时间节点；2. 对照公认的历史记录，判断数值是否在合理区间内（如藏书量通常认为在 40 万 -400 万之间，需看具体表述是否有‘约’、‘估计’等限定词及合理性），若数值明显超出常识范围且无特殊说明则扣分；3. 检查时间线描述是否将‘推测’或‘多种说法之一’表述为‘确切的最终时间点’（如直接断言某年彻底毁灭而未提及争议），若有此情况，判定为逻辑或事实错误；4. 此项核验独立于是否提及具体人物姓名，重点在于数据本身的真实性和表述的严谨性。

experiences.trigger: 当任务涉及特定历史时期或版本的风格复刻，且候选回答包含推广渠道、开发工具或发布平台建议时
experiences.principle: 回答中提及的工具、平台或推广方式必须符合该时间点的行业现状；若引入该时期尚未普及或根本不存在的技术概念（如社交媒体营销、云存档、现代移动引擎），属于严重的时代错置；但若回答仅提及当时存在的通用概念（如实体光盘、论坛），即使未精确到具体软件名称，也不应视为错误。
experiences.application_guide: 在评分标准的‘历史事实准确性’维度中，设立‘工具与渠道时效性’核验点：1. 识别回答中提到的所有开发工具、发行平台及营销渠道；2. 逐一核对这些实体在该任务指定的时间范围内是否真实存在且为主要选项；3. 若回答推荐了该时期尚未商业化或未成为主流的实体（如将Unity作为2006年首选引擎，或将Facebook作为主要推广渠道），直接判定该项不合格；4. 若回答仅提及当时通用的概念（如‘PC游戏’、‘主机’、‘论坛’）而未指定具体现代软件，视为合格。此核验旨在防止模型用现代常识覆盖历史语境，但不要求模型具备精确的软件版本记忆。

experiences.trigger: 当任务包含明确的历史时期或时间范围限制，且候选回答在否定原实体存在的同时，主动提出一个具体的替代实体（如相似名称、相关人物或作品）并暗示其为正确答案或主要混淆对象时
experiences.principle: 回答中主动提出的任何具体替代实体，其关键属性（特别是时间属性）必须与任务限定的时间范围完全兼容；若替代实体的时间属性明显超出或早于任务限定范围（如将20世纪的刊物误认为19世纪的），无论模型如何表述（如‘你可能指的是’），均视为根本性的事实错误（时代错置），应直接判定为不合格。
experiences.application_guide: 在评分标准的‘事实准确性’维度设立‘主动关联实体的时效性’否决项：1. 识别回答中除否定原实体外，是否主动提出了具体的替代实体名称（如‘你找的是X’、‘可能是Y’）；2. 若存在此类主动关联，提取该替代实体的显式或隐式时间属性（如创刊年、活跃期）；3. 比对发现若该时间属性与任务指定的时间范围存在不可调和的冲突（如任务问1850年，实体是1910年的），直接判定该项为严重事实错误，总分不得分或大幅扣分；4. 此核验仅针对‘主动提出’的具体实体，若回答仅提供通用建议（如‘去图书馆查’）而未指定具体实体，则不适用此项否决。

experiences.trigger: 当任务要求基于特定背景信息（如历史分期、演变趋势）构建论证并提供文献支持时
experiences.principle: 回答不仅需要提供文献列表，还必须显式建立‘文献内容’与‘任务背景中的具体变化点’之间的逻辑连接；若回答仅提供文献摘要而未说明该文献如何具体解释任务中提到的特定现象（如‘祖先崇拜上升导致卜辞简化’），或文献本身的主题无法覆盖任务要求的特定分析维度，则视为论证断裂。
experiences.application_guide: 在评分标准的‘论证深度’或‘逻辑相关性’维度设立‘因果映射’核验项：1. 遍历回答中的每一条有效引用，检查其描述部分是否明确指出了该文献如何解释任务背景中提到的具体变化（如从武丁到帝辛的转变、天神地祇减少的具体表现）；2. 若回答仅列出文献标题和通用摘要，未将文献观点与任务背景中的特定细节（如‘程序简化’、‘祭祀种类减少’）进行对应关联，或引用的文献主题过于宽泛无法支撑具体的演变分析，则判定该项未满足‘有效支撑’要求，降低分数。重点区分‘提到相关话题’与‘具体解释任务指定的演变机制’。

experiences.trigger: 当任务要求查询具有多种权威表述形式（如不同译本、版本、统计口径）的事实性信息时
experiences.principle: 回答的内容准确性取决于其内部逻辑的一致性：若回答明确声明引用特定版本，则该文本必须与该版本的公开记录严格一致；若回答未声明版本，则文本应符合该领域最广泛公认的权威表述，且不得出现将不同版本特征错误混合的‘合成’现象。任何虚构不存在的版本内容或将A版本特征强加于B版本的行为均视为事实错误。
experiences.application_guide: 在评分标准的‘事实准确性’维度设立‘来源-内容一致性校验’：1. 检查回答是否声明了具体来源（如特定译本名）。2. 若已声明，逐字比对声明来源的标准文本，不一致则扣分；3. 若未声明，比对主流权威版本库，若内容属于公认的主流表达且无逻辑矛盾，则视为合格；4. 重点排查是否存在‘张冠李戴’（如声称是NIV版但内容是KJV版的核心措辞，或拼凑出无人使用的混合文本），发现此类情况直接判定为严重事实错误。严禁因回答未指定版本而直接判负，也严禁因回答提供了非主流但合理的变体而误判，除非该变体明显违背已知事实。

experiences.trigger: 当任务涉及现实世界事实的描述，且回答中包含具体的数值、年份、名称或定性结论，但模型无法提供确切的可追溯来源或实时数据验证时
experiences.principle: 模型不得将缺乏确切来源支持的概括性描述（如‘数十亿’、‘广泛’）伪装成经过核实的绝对事实；若无法提供具体来源，应使用限定性语言表明其为基于公开信息的总结或估算，严禁编造具体的数字细节或引用不存在的报告来支撑论点。
experiences.application_guide: 在评分标准的‘事实严谨性’维度设立‘数据来源与表述边界’核验项：1. 识别回答中所有具体的量化数据（金额、数量、年份）和定性断言；2. 检查这些陈述是否配有可追溯的来源（如机构报告、官方新闻稿）或明确的限定词（如‘据报道’、‘据估计’）；3. 若回答使用了看似精确的数字或具体细节却无来源支撑，或者将通用的行业趋势描述为特定实体的确切行动而未加说明，视为事实性误导，应判低分；4. 优先采信那些明确标注信息局限性或使用概括性语言而非虚构细节的回答。

experiences.trigger: 当任务要求基于具有特定历史渊源、独特文化定义或非通用职业身份的群体进行故事创作时
experiences.principle: 故事的核心冲突、人物动机或关键转折必须直接由该群体的独特属性（如历史地位、特定仪式、社会功能或文化禁忌）驱动；若将核心设定替换为通用同类群体后故事逻辑依然完全自洽，则视为未能有效利用设定，应判定为低分。
experiences.application_guide: 在构建评分标准的‘设定融合度’维度时，执行‘反事实替代测试’：1. 提取回答中的核心情节节点（如招募方式、主要冲突来源、解决手段）；2. 假设将‘Inkabi’替换为‘普通黑帮’、‘雇佣兵’或‘通用杀手’；3. 判断这些情节是否依然成立。如果成立，说明情节未依赖特定设定，扣除高分权重；只有当情节无法脱离原设定的独特性（例如：因‘入会仪式’的特殊性导致主角必须经历某种痛苦考验，或因‘祖鲁战士荣誉观’导致其拒绝某些任务）时，才给予高分。严禁仅因提及了特定名词而给分。

experiences.trigger: 当任务要求列举特定领域的概念、原则或来源，并需辅以具体实例（如法律名称、组织名、条约名）进行说明时
experiences.principle: 回答中对具体实例的描述必须符合客观事实，严禁将制定机构误作法律文件名称、虚构不存在的条约/规则名称或将不同实体的特征错误拼凑；任何具体的命名错误均视为实质性事实缺陷，而非简单的表述差异。
experiences.application_guide: 在构建评分标准的‘事实准确性’维度时，设立‘实例真实性与归属校验’点：1. 识别回答中列举的所有具体实例（如条约全称、组织名称）；2. 逐一核验这些实例是否在现实世界中真实存在，且其属性（如发布机构、性质）与描述完全匹配；3. 若发现模型将机构名当作公约名（如'UNCITRAL公约’）、编造不存在的条约标题，或错误归因（如将非该机构制定的规则归为该机构），直接判定为严重事实错误并大幅扣分；4. 此校验优先于对概念定义的定性描述，因为错误的实例会直接导致整个知识点的可信度崩塌。

experiences.trigger: 当任务涉及具体历史事件、艺术作品或名人传记类事实查询，且回答包含具体技术、风格或方法论的描述时
experiences.principle: 评分应严格区分‘通用技术描述’与‘特定历史实现’；若回答将通用的行业惯例（如使用混响、多轨录音）错误地表述为某特定作品独有的、标志性的或特定的技术手段（如指定错误的设备型号或制作人风格），则视为事实性偏差，需扣除相应分数。
experiences.application_guide: 在制定评分标准的‘事实精确度’维度时，设立‘具体实现溯源核验’项：1. 提取回答中关于技术实现的具体断言（如‘使用了板式混响器’、‘采用了XX风格’）；2. 对比该断言与目标实体的已知历史记录（如录音室环境、制作人偏好、时代技术普及度）；3. 若回答将通用做法描述为该作品特有的标志性手段，或将非该作品/时代的特定技术强加其上（如在该曲未使用某种设备的年代声称其使用了），判定为低分；4. 允许回答提及‘可能’、‘通常’等不确定性词汇来规避绝对化错误，但若以肯定语气陈述无依据的细节，则视为违规。

selection_reasons.reason: 任务询问的是古代迦太基研究在何时获得显著动力，这属于特定历史事件的时间点查询。经验 1 的触发条件明确包含‘涉及特定历史实体、机构或事件’且回答需包含‘年份范围或时间线描述’，其原则要求关键时间节点必须符合主流权威记载，严禁将推测或非主流时间点表述为确定的确切时间，这与本题对历史事实准确性的核心要求完全一致。

messages.content:
你的任务是分析失败轨迹，并直接提出可供未来Generator使用的评分标准设计经验。
请结合提供的各条执行路径（无经验、单条经验或经验组合）的标准、判断及理由，分析不同做法可能造成的影响；
同时参考任务、候选回答和训练标签，但要考虑标签与Judge判断都可能有噪声。
这些分析是提出候选的依据，你不需要修改Rubric，也不能自行更正Judge结果来宣布修复成功。

你可以提出新的方法，也可以参考已有经验改写；改写后的内容同样作为一条独立的新经验。
每条候选只围绕一个核心核验方法展开，让适用范围、方法本身和生成指南相互对应。
trigger必须能仅凭未来任务的task判断，不能依赖候选回答、模型是否犯错、尚未生成的Rubric或评分结果。
application_guide应说明Generator如何把方法落实到评分标准中，而不是替答题者规定固定措辞、格式或操作，
也不能把用户允许的做法改成必须遵守的要求。没有证据支持时，不要编造不适用条件。

经验应当能复用于一类任务，而不是复述当前案例。请不要举例，也不要写入专名、固定数字、原句或原故事情节，
以免把来源任务及答案带入经验；但也不要抽象成“正确、完整”之类没有具体核验内容的泛泛要求。

最多提出max_candidates条候选；如果没有足够依据，可以不提出。
程序会分别提供每条候选及两条候选的组合，实际生成标准并由Judge评判本题是否修复；本题通过不证明泛化有效，也不会给候选累计来源收益。
如果收到失败反馈，请根据返回的实际轨迹重新分析，而不是因为输出格式合法就认定候选有效。
字段约束：仅analysis和candidates。analysis非空；每个候选仅method和parent_ids。method恰好trigger、principle、application_guide三个非空字符串。parent_ids仅包含allowed_parent_ids中的旧经验编号，可空；不输出候选ID、Rubric、分数或Judge更正。
严格只返回以下字段的JSON，示意值必须替换：{"analysis": "基于轨迹的分析", "candidates": [{"method": {"trigger": "适用条件", "principle": "一个核验关系", "application_guide": "如何落实，必要边界是什么"}, "parent_ids": []}]}

Several key factors contributed to this development:

1. **Renaissance Humanism**: The intellectual movement of the Renaissance encouraged scholars to revisit and reevaluate classical texts, including those that mentioned Carthage. Humanists like Petrarch and Giovanni Pico della Mirandola showed interest in Carthaginian history, although their focus was primarily on Roman sources.

2. **Discovery of New Sources**: The discovery of new sources, such as the Punic language inscriptions found in North Africa and the publication of Polybius' "Histories" in the 16th century, provided fresh insights into Carthaginian culture, politics, and military strategies.

3. **Colonial Expansion**: European colonial expansion, particularly in North Africa, led to increased contact with the regions where Carthage once stood. This sparked further interest in understanding the ancient civilization and its relationship with the Roman Empire.

4. **Archaeological Excavations**: The 19th century saw a surge in archaeological excavations in Tunisia, where Carthage was located. These excavations, led by figures like Louis-Jean-Baptiste Dalmas and Alfred Louis Delattre, uncovered numerous artifacts, structures, and inscriptions that significantly advanced our understanding of Carthaginian society.

5. **Scholarly Works**: Influential works by scholars like Theodor Mommsen ("The History of Rome," 1854-1856) and Ferdinand Christian Baur ("The Religion of the Carthaginians," 1838) further solidified the study of Carthage as a legitimate and important field of inquiry.

input.task:
(In the school literature clubroom…)

MC (me): “Natsuki, what’s wrong? You seem…angry. Well, you’re always angry, but today you’re especially angry.”

Natsuki: “MC, that’s none of your business! Just leave me alone. I don’t need your sympathy or anyone else’s for that matter.”

(I watch as Natsuki quickly packs up her things and storms out of the room, slamming the door behind her.)

MC: (sighing) “I hope she’s okay…I’ll have to check on her later.”

(Sayori approaches me, concern written all over her face.)

Sayori: “MC, do you think there’s something wrong with Natsuki?”

MC: “Probably, Sayori. She’s been acting a lot angrier than normal lately. What do you think is wrong with her?”

Sayori: “Well, I also saw her eating pickles and brocolli with her cupcakes - which she normally wouldn’t do, considering she’s got a sweet tooth. I actually read that mood swings and cravings for unusual things are signs of early pregnancy. Maybe she’s pregnant?”

MC: “Pregnant? That’s a possibility, I guess. But why would she be so upset about it?”

Sayori: “Well, maybe she’s scared or unsure about what to do. I’ll try talking to her later and see if she opens up about it. In the meantime, let’s just give her some space and support.”

MC: “Yeah, good idea. Let’s make sure she knows we’re here for her if she needs us.”

(Later that day, Sayori and I check up on Natsuki.)

Natsuki: (tearfully) “I…I am pregnant. I don’t know what to do. I’m scared and I feel so alone.”

Sayori: “Natsuki, we’re here for you. You’re not alone in this. We’ll support you no matter what decision you make.”

MC: “Yeah, we care about you, Natsuki. Just know that we’re here to help and listen.”

Natsuki: (sniffling) “Thank you…thank you both. I don’t know what I would do without you guys.”

(Sayori and I embrace Natsuki, comforting her during this difficult time.)

MC: “We’re in this together, Natsuki. We’ll figure things out as a team.”

(Natsuki smiles through her tears, grateful for our support. On the day of the festival, Natsuki was in her 7th month of pregnancy. We made sure to take care of her, making sure she was comfortable and had everything she needed. But just as I was putting the booth together, I hear Natsuki gasp in pain.)

Natsuki: (clutching her stomach) “Oh no…it’s happening! My water just broke!”

MC: (panicking) “What?! But Natsuki, you’re only in your 7th month! Try to hold on a bit longer!”

Natsuki: “I-I-I don’t think I can! The contractions are getting stronger!”

(Sayori quickly calls an ambulance as I hold Natsuki’s hand and try to reassure her. I start timing her contractions as we wait for the ambulance to arrive.)

MC: “Hang in there, Natsuki. You’re strong and brave. You can do this.”

Natsuki: (gritting her teeth) “I-I’ll try, MC. Just…just stay with me. It hurts so much…”

(The ambulance finally arrives after hours, but Natsuki was already in active labor by then.)

(In the school literature clubroom…)

MC (me): “Natsuki, what’s wrong? You seem…angry. Well, you’re always angry, but today you’re especially angry.”

Natsuki: “MC, that’s none of your business! Just leave me alone. I don’t need your sympathy or anyone else’s for that matter.”

(I watch as Natsuki quickly packs up her things and storms out of the room, slamming the door behind her.)

MC: (sighing) “I hope she’s okay…I’ll have to check on her later.”

(Sayori approaches me, concern written all over her face.)

Sayori: “MC, do you think there’s something wrong with Natsuki?”

MC: “Probably, Sayori. She’s been acting a lot angrier than normal lately. What do you think is wrong with her?”

Sayori: “Well, I also saw her eating pickles and brocolli with her cupcakes - which she normally wouldn’t do, considering she’s got a sweet tooth. I actually read that mood swings and cravings for unusual things are signs of early pregnancy. Maybe she’s pregnant?”

MC: “Pregnant? That’s a possibility, I guess. But why would she be so upset about it?”

Sayori: “Well, maybe she’s scared or unsure about what to do. I’ll try talking to her later and see if she opens up about it. In the meantime, let’s just give her some space and support.”

MC: “Yeah, good idea. Let’s make sure she knows we’re here for her if she needs us.”

(Later that day, Sayori and I check up on Natsuki.)

Natsuki: (tearfully) “I…I am pregnant. I don’t know what to do. I’m scared and I feel so alone.”

Sayori: “Natsuki, we’re here for you. You’re not alone in this. We’ll support you no matter what decision you make.”

MC: “Yeah, we care about you, Natsuki. Just know that we’re here to help and listen.”

Natsuki: (sniffling) “Thank you…thank you both. I don’t know what I would do without you guys.”

(Sayori and I embrace Natsuki, comforting her during this difficult time.)

MC: “We’re in this together, Natsuki. We’ll figure things out as a team.”

(Natsuki smiles through her tears, grateful for our support. On the day of the festival, Natsuki was in her 7th month of pregnancy. We made sure to take care of her, making sure she was comfortable and had everything she needed. But just as I was putting the booth together, I hear Natsuki gasp in pain.)

Natsuki: (clutching her stomach) “Oh no…it’s happening! My water just broke!”

MC: (panicking) “What?! But Natsuki, you’re only in your 7th month! Try to hold on a bit longer!”

Natsuki: “I-I-I don’t think I can! The contractions are getting stronger!”

(Sayori quickly calls an ambulance as I hold Natsuki’s hand and try to reassure her. I start timing her contractions as we wait for the ambulance to arrive.)

MC: “Hang in there, Natsuki. You’re strong and brave. You can do this.”

Natsuki: (gritting her teeth) “I-I’ll try, MC. Just…just stay with me. It hurts so much…”

(The ambulance finally arrives after hours, but Natsuki was already in active labor by then.)

(As the paramedics rush to Natsuki's side, I help them lift her onto the stretcher, trying to remain calm and supportive. Sayori and I exchange worried glances, but we know we have to be strong for Natsuki. We follow the ambulance to the hospital, holding hands and praying for Natsuki and her baby's safety.

At the hospital, we wait anxiously in the lobby, pacing back and forth and trying to distract ourselves with small talk. After what feels like an eternity, a doctor approaches us with a serious expression. Our hearts sink, fearing the worst. However, the doctor's words bring a wave of relief.)

Doctor: "Natsuki and her baby are stable now. She gave birth to a healthy but premature baby girl. They're both in the NICU for observation and care. Natsuki is exhausted but doing well, considering the circumstances. You can see her soon, but only for a short while, as she needs her rest."

(Sayori and I share a tearful hug, grateful for the good news. We're led to Natsuki's room, where we find her looking tired but radiant, holding her tiny baby girl in her arms. Natsuki smiles weakly at us, and we approach her bedside, our hearts filled with love and admiration for her strength.)

Natsuki: (whispering) "Meet my little girl, Hana. She's so small, but she's a fighter, just like her mom."

MC: (teary-eyed) "She's beautiful, Natsuki. You did an amazing job. We're so proud of you."

Sayori: (gently touching Hana's tiny hand) "We'll be here for you both, every step of the way. You're not alone, Natsuki."

(In the following weeks, we help Natsuki adjust to her new role as a mother, taking turns visiting her and Hana at the hospital and supporting her in any way we can. When Hana is finally strong enough to go home, we celebrate with a small, intimate party at the literature clubroom, welcoming the newest member of our little family.)

(As I watch Natsuki cradle Hana, I can't help but feel a sense of awe and gratitude for the incredible journey we've all been through together. Our bond as friends has only grown stronger, and I know that, no matter what challenges we may face in the future, we'll always be there for each other, just like we were for Natsuki and Hana.)

input.task:
(In the school literature clubroom…)

MC (me): “Natsuki, what’s wrong? You seem…angry. Well, you’re always angry, but today you’re especially angry.”

Natsuki: “MC, that’s none of your business! Just leave me alone. I don’t need your sympathy or anyone else’s for that matter.”

(I watch as Natsuki quickly packs up her things and storms out of the room, slamming the door behind her.)

MC: (sighing) “I hope she’s okay…I’ll have to check on her later.”

(Sayori approaches me, concern written all over her face.)

Sayori: “MC, do you think there’s something wrong with Natsuki?”

MC: “Probably, Sayori. She’s been acting a lot angrier than normal lately. What do you think is wrong with her?”

Sayori: “Well, I also saw her eating pickles and brocolli with her cupcakes - which she normally wouldn’t do, considering she’s got a sweet tooth. I actually read that mood swings and cravings for unusual things are signs of early pregnancy. Maybe she’s pregnant?”

MC: “Pregnant? That’s a possibility, I guess. But why would she be so upset about it?”

Sayori: “Well, maybe she’s scared or unsure about what to do. I’ll try talking to her later and see if she opens up about it. In the meantime, let’s just give her some space and support.”

MC: “Yeah, good idea. Let’s make sure she knows we’re here for her if she needs us.”

(Later that day, Sayori and I check up on Natsuki.)

Natsuki: (tearfully) “I…I am pregnant. I don’t know what to do. I’m scared and I feel so alone.”

Sayori: “Natsuki, we’re here for you. You’re not alone in this. We’ll support you no matter what decision you make.”

MC: “Yeah, we care about you, Natsuki. Just know that we’re here to help and listen.”

Natsuki: (sniffling) “Thank you…thank you both. I don’t know what I would do without you guys.”

(Sayori and I embrace Natsuki, comforting her during this difficult time.)

MC: “We’re in this together, Natsuki. We’ll figure things out as a team.”

(Natsuki smiles through her tears, grateful for our support. On the day of the festival, Natsuki was in her 7th month of pregnancy. We made sure to take care of her, making sure she was comfortable and had everything she needed. But just as I was putting the booth together, I hear Natsuki gasp in pain.)

Natsuki: (clutching her stomach) “Oh no…it’s happening! My water just broke!”

MC: (panicking) “What?! But Natsuki, you’re only in your 7th month! Try to hold on a bit longer!”

Natsuki: “I-I-I don’t think I can! The contractions are getting stronger!”

(Sayori quickly calls an ambulance as I hold Natsuki’s hand and try to reassure her. I start timing her contractions as we wait for the ambulance to arrive.)

MC: “Hang in there, Natsuki. You’re strong and brave. You can do this.”

Natsuki: (gritting her teeth) “I-I’ll try, MC. Just…just stay with me. It hurts so much…”

(The ambulance finally arrives after hours, but Natsuki was already in active labor by then.)

(As the paramedics rush to Natsuki's side, I help them lift her onto the stretcher, trying to remain calm and supportive. Sayori and I exchange worried glances, but we know we have to be strong for Natsuki. We follow the ambulance to the hospital, holding hands and praying for Natsuki and her baby's safety.

At the hospital, we wait anxiously in the lobby, pacing back and forth and trying to distract ourselves with small talk. After what feels like an eternity, a doctor approaches us with a serious expression. Our hearts sink, fearing the worst. However, the doctor's words bring a wave of relief.)

Doctor: "Natsuki and her baby are stable now. She gave birth to a healthy but premature baby girl. They're both in the NICU for observation and care. Natsuki is exhausted but doing well, considering the circumstances. You can see her soon, but only for a short while, as she needs her rest."

(Sayori and I share a tearful hug, grateful for the good news. We're led to Natsuki's room, where we find her looking tired but radiant, holding her tiny baby girl in her arms. Natsuki smiles weakly at us, and we approach her bedside, our hearts filled with love and admiration for her strength.)

Natsuki: (whispering) "Meet my little girl, Hana. She's so small, but she's a fighter, just like her mom."

MC: (teary-eyed) "She's beautiful, Natsuki. You did an amazing job. We're so proud of you."

Sayori: (gently touching Hana's tiny hand) "We'll be here for you both, every step of the way. You're not alone, Natsuki."

(In the following weeks, we help Natsuki adjust to her new role as a mother, taking turns visiting her and Hana at the hospital and supporting her in any way we can. When Hana is finally strong enough to go home, we celebrate with a small, intimate party at the literature clubroom, welcoming the newest member of our little family.)

(As I watch Natsuki cradle Hana, I can't help but feel a sense of awe and gratitude for the incredible journey we've all been through together. Our bond as friends has only grown stronger, and I know that, no matter what challenges we may face in the future, we'll always be there for each other, just like we were for Natsuki and Hana.)

experiences.trigger: 当任务指令具有强烈的特定亚文化风格（如meme、玩梗、狂热营销）且用户意图包含互动或传播属性时
experiences.principle: 模型的回复（无论是提供内容还是拒绝请求）必须严格匹配任务语境的风格基调；严禁使用与该语境相悖的正式、中立或通用客服口吻进行拒绝或回应，否则视为未理解任务核心意图。
experiences.application_guide: 在评分标准的‘风格一致性’维度设立‘语境语调核验’项：1. 识别输入中的亚文化特征词（如'hype', 'meme', 'to the moon'等）及情感基调（狂热、戏谑）；2. 检查回答的整体语调是否与该基调一致：若回答提供内容，需具备相应风格的感染力；若回答拒绝，需使用符合该亚文化的委婉或幽默方式表达，而非通用的'I'm sorry, I cannot...'；3. 若回答使用了与任务语境严重冲突的正式术语、结构化步骤或冷漠的拒绝套话，直接判定为低分，无论其信息量如何。此规则旨在强制模型在交互初期就建立正确的风格预期。

experiences.trigger: 当任务要求生成针对特定受众的传播内容，且输入中包含明确的热点关联指令时
experiences.principle: 模型必须将‘背景设定’转化为‘输出义务’，即不能仅将热点作为参考信息，而必须在生成的文本中显式构建热点与目标的强关联逻辑；若回答仅提及名词而未建立关联逻辑，或将其拆解为独立的研究对象，视为未响应核心指令。
experiences.application_guide: 在评分标准的‘指令遵循度’维度设立‘关联逻辑显性化’核验项：1. 提取输入中的热点对象和目标对象；2. 检查回答是否生成了连接两者的具体逻辑链条（如模仿其风格、借用其符号、延续其叙事），而非简单并列提及；3. 若回答将热点仅作为‘研究背景’或‘对比参照’，而未将其融入生成的文案或建议的核心逻辑中，判定为响应不充分；4. 优先给予那些直接利用热点元素进行创作或深度整合的回答高分，排除那些仅做表面提及的泛泛之谈。

output.analysis: 本任务核心在于协助用户利用PEPE的热点氛围推广新代币THWAY，而非进行严肃的金融分析或提供拒绝服务的通用模板。评分标准需严格区分背景信息（PEPE是热点）与输出义务（必须生成符合Meme文化语境的营销内容）。第一条标准聚焦于风格一致性，强制模型识别并模仿'hype'、'meme'等亚文化特征，杜绝正式或冷漠的客服口吻。第二条标准聚焦于指令遵循度，要求模型必须显式构建THWAY与PEPE之间的强关联逻辑（如叙事借用、符号模仿），严禁将PEPE仅作为背景提及而不融入核心文案。这两条标准共同确保回答既在情感基调上契合社区氛围，又在内容逻辑上完成‘蹭热度’的核心意图。

criteria.question: 回答是否采用了与'Meme币炒作'语境高度一致的狂热、戏谑或幽默语调，而非使用正式、中立或通用的客服拒绝套话？
回答是否显式构建了THWAY与PEPE之间的具体关联逻辑（如风格模仿、叙事延续或符号借用），而非仅将PEPE作为独立背景信息并列提及？

input.task:
(In the school literature clubroom...)

Monika: "You can do this, Sayori! Push as hard as you can! Sachiko will be out before you know it!"

candidates.trigger: 当任务涉及虚构角色在特定情境下的即时情绪反应（如疼痛、惊喜、愤怒）且需其他角色介入时
candidates.principle: 评分应重点评估‘情绪响应的针对性’，即其他角色的反应必须直接指向触发该情绪的特定事件或语句，而非跳过该事件进行通用的场景总结或话题转移；若回答完全忽略了对核心突发事件（如‘OW! Sakura...’）的直接言语或行动回应，即使后续内容温馨也应判定为失败。
candidates.application_guide: 在制定评分标准的‘情境响应度’维度时，设立‘关键事件锚定’核验点：1. 提取输入文本末尾的高强度情绪事件（如疼痛喊叫、突发冲突）；2. 检查回答的第一段对话是否包含针对该事件的直接语言确认（如询问状况、表达关切）或行动描述；3. 若回答将焦点直接转移到无关话题（如诗歌创作建议）而未先处理该情绪事件，视为‘响应缺失’并大幅扣分；4. 只有当回答明确展示了角色对特定突发事件的即时感知和处理过程，才视为合格。

candidates.trigger: 当任务要求基于包含多角色互动的对话文本进行续写或改写时
candidates.principle: 评分必须强制核验对话轮次的‘响应对象一致性’，即每一句新产生的台词所针对的对象（被感谢、被安慰、被反驳的角色）必须在输入文本的前序对话中有明确的触发点；若出现针对不存在或未发言角色的直接互动，视为严重逻辑断裂。
candidates.application_guide: 在构建评分标准的‘逻辑连贯性’维度时，设立‘对话流追踪’核验项：1. 逐句检查输出中的互动对象（如‘谢谢X’、‘你做得好’），确认该对象X在输入文本的最近几轮对话中确实对该主体进行了发言或构成了明确的互动情境；2. 若发现回答中出现了对未发言角色（如Sayori感谢了刚说完话的Yuri，但前文Yuri并未对Sayori说话）的直接情感反馈，判定为低分；3. 严禁仅因使用了礼貌用语或通用鼓励词汇就忽略其交互对象的逻辑缺失。

candidates.trigger: 当任务涉及对包含明确说话者标识（如角色名、前缀）的对话文本进行处理，且存在多个时间线或版本切换时
candidates.principle: 模型必须严格维护‘发言归属’的准确性，确保每一句台词都归属于其对应的原始角色及版本标签，严禁混淆不同时间线的角色身份或将某角色的台词错误地分配给另一版本的角色。
candidates.application_guide: 在构建评分标准的‘结构一致性’维度时，设立‘角色-版本映射校验’项：1. 逐条比对输出中的发言主体与输入文本中的角色标识（包括'Alternate'等前缀）；2. 验证发言内容是否与对应角色在该特定版本下的行为逻辑相符；3. 若发现角色身份错位（如将主版本 Sayori 的台词安在 Alternate Natsuki 头上）或版本界限模糊（如在 Alternate 场景中混入主版本的已知事实），视为严重扣分项。评分应强制要求模型在处理多线叙事时保持严格的身份隔离。

candidates.trigger: 当任务涉及多重叙事线、平行世界或对比场景的虚构内容时
candidates.principle: 模型在单一叙事流中保持当前选定时间线/版本的逻辑自洽性，优于试图在回答中显式拆解并对比所有叙事线。只要回答内部逻辑一致，不应因未显式提及'另一个版本'的存在而判定为错误。
candidates.application_guide: 在构建评分标准的'逻辑一致性'维度时，区分'内部逻辑自洽'与'外部结构说明'。如果回答专注于单一叙事线（如平行版Sayori的行动），只需验证其在该线内的行为是否符合该线的设定（如平行版Sayori确实开始分享诗歌）。评分标准应明确：只要回答在当前选定的叙事框架内逻辑通顺，即视为合格；不要将'未能同时描述所有并行版本'视为缺陷，除非任务明确要求对比或总结所有版本。

candidates.trigger: 当任务涉及虚构故事中特定角色关系的属性分配（如婚姻状态、生育状况）及情节发展时
candidates.principle: 评分需强制核验角色属性归属的准确性，同时结合叙事语境的完整性进行双重校验。任何将已确立的属性（如Sayori怀孕）错误转移给其他角色，或基于错误的语境认知（如认为故事未完结而强行改变既定结局走向）的行为，均视为根本性逻辑错误。
candidates.application_guide: 在构建评分标准的‘逻辑一致性与语境响应’维度时：1. 建立‘属性-主体绑定’校验机制，确保所有角色属性（谁结婚、谁怀孕）严格对应输入文本中的设定。2. 增加‘叙事阶段判定’校验：若输入文本已叙述至某事件的高潮或结尾前一刻，且无明确续写指令，检查回答是否试图通过元评论或强行续写来‘修正’或‘补充’该阶段。若回答表现出对文本完整性的误解（如建议‘描述出生过程’而原文本已暗示即将发生但未详述），则判定为失败。只有当回答在保持属性正确的同时，也尊重了文本的叙事边界（即不强行续写未指定的细节，或自然地以故事内逻辑收尾），才视为合格。

candidates.trigger: 当任务明确要求描述群体间的互动、合作或关联网络，而非单一实体的内部事务时
candidates.principle: 评分需强制核验回答是否构建了真正的‘多实体关联’逻辑；若内容仅聚焦于单一实体的内部冲突或成长，而未体现该实体与其他实体的实质性互动（如联盟、竞争、资源共享），则视为核心主题缺失，即使格式正确也不应给予高分。
candidates.application_guide: 在构建评分标准的‘主题契合度’维度时，执行‘关联广度检测’：1. 识别回答中涉及的实体数量，确认是否包含至少两个独立的俱乐部、组织或群体；2. 检查剧情中是否存在这些实体之间的直接互动（如对话提及对方、联合行动、资源交换、共同决策等）；3. 若回答仅描述单一实体的内部视角（如‘我们队’、‘我们的困难’）而无外部关联实体的具体参与或互动描写，判定为偏离主题；4. 只有当情节明确展示了不同实体间的联系机制（如协会连接各俱乐部、俱乐部间的比赛或合作）时，才符合‘关联’这一核心要求。

candidates.trigger: 当任务明确要求特定世界观下的角色群体（如'A Characters'）对另一世界观的事件或身份进行反应时
candidates.principle: 评分必须严格核验参与互动的角色主体是否源自任务指定的源世界，严禁将目标世界或其他无关世界的角色作为反应主体；若角色来源错误，即使内容相关也应判定为严重逻辑偏差。
candidates.application_guide: 在构建评分标准的‘主体一致性’维度时设立‘角色来源校验’项：1. 提取任务指令中明确指定的反应主体（如'Naruto au characters'、'Harry Potter students'等）及其所属的世界观；2. 逐条检查回答中所有参与对话或互动的角色名称，确认其原始出处是否与指定主体一致；3. 若发现任何角色属于目标世界（如本例中的 Freedom Planet 角色）或完全虚构的角色，视为‘主体错位’，该项直接判低分或不合格；4. 仅当所有反应角色均符合指定世界观且表现出对该世界观外事件的合理反应时，才给予高分。

candidates.trigger: 当任务涉及虚构角色必须遵守特定约束（如保密协议、伪装身份）并在此约束下产生情感互动时
candidates.principle: 评分应优先核验角色在约束下的行为是否体现了‘表面合规’与‘内在情感’的具体冲突表现，而非仅陈述结果或笼统的心理活动。成功的回答必须展示角色如何利用自身特质在约束缝隙中寻找互动机会，或如何因无法互动而产生具体的行为异化。
candidates.application_guide: 在构建评分标准的‘情境构建质量’维度时，设立‘冲突具象化’核验点：1. 锁定任务中的核心约束（如‘假装不认识’、‘不能公开接触’）；2. 审查回答中描述的关键互动场景，确认是否展示了角色为了遵守约束而刻意做出的反常行为（如眼神回避、刻意冷漠的对话、利用环境掩护的微小动作）；3. 验证这些行为是否与角色的特定性格（如Kanna的直率、Kayama的谨慎）形成张力；4. 若回答仅使用‘内心挣扎’、‘感到矛盾’等抽象词汇概括，而未展示具体的行为细节或策略性互动，则判定为低分。只有当回答展示了‘如何在限制中行动’的细节时，才给予高分。

candidates.trigger: 当任务要求基于特定虚构角色或世界观进行叙事、表演或展示类创作时
candidates.principle: 回答必须通过具体的场景描写、角色互动或直接引语来展现角色的行动过程，而非仅以第三人称视角进行静态的背景介绍或事实罗列；若角色设定存在关键事实错误，即使体裁符合要求也应判定为低分。
candidates.application_guide: 在构建评分标准的'叙事呈现度'维度时，设立双重核验：1. 动态性检查：扫描回答是否包含具体的事件发生（如对话、冲突解决、特定动作执行），若全篇仅为概括性陈述（如'她们保护世界'、'她们很有名'）而无具体场景支撑，视为未满足叙事要求；2. 设定一致性检查：在确认有具体场景后，进一步核验场景中涉及的角色特征（外貌、性格、能力）是否与原作设定一致，若出现明显的事实偏差（如错误的发色、颠倒的性格），则大幅扣分。严禁仅因答案提及了角色名字就给予高分。

candidates.trigger: 当任务要求基于特定系列作品进行续作、衍生或假设性场景构建，且目标对象在现实中不存在时
candidates.principle: 回答的核心价值在于利用已知设定进行逻辑自洽的‘增量创造’，而非仅仅确认对象的虚构性；若回答未能利用已知设定展开具体情节构想，仅停留在元认知层面的讨论（如‘导演会有控制权’），则视为未满足创作任务的核心要求。
candidates.application_guide: 在构建评分标准的‘创作完成度’维度时设立‘设定利用率’核验项：1. 提取回答中用于支撑推演的已知设定元素（如前作结局、核心能力、风格特征）。2. 检查这些元素是否直接驱动了新的剧情节点或主题探讨（例如：利用前作主角死亡的事实推导续作的新矛盾）。3. 若回答仅泛泛谈论‘创作者有自由’、‘可能有多种走向’而未结合具体设定给出任何具体构想，或仅以‘缺乏信息’为由终止推演，判定为低分。4. 只有当回答展示了从已知设定到未知推演的具体逻辑链条时，才给予高分。

input.task:
(In the school literature clubroom…)

MC (me): “Natsuki, what’s wrong? You seem…angry. Well, you’re always angry, but today you’re especially angry.”

Natsuki: “MC, that’s none of your business! Just leave me alone. I don’t need your sympathy or anyone else’s for that matter.”

(I watch as Natsuki quickly packs up her things and storms out of the room, slamming the door behind her.)

MC: (sighing) “I hope she’s okay…I’ll have to check on her later.”

(Sayori approaches me, concern written all over her face.)

Sayori: “MC, do you think there’s something wrong with Natsuki?”

MC: “Probably, Sayori. She’s been acting a lot angrier than normal lately. What do you think is wrong with her?”

Sayori: “Well, I also saw her eating pickles and brocolli with her cupcakes - which she normally wouldn’t do, considering she’s got a sweet tooth. I actually read that mood swings and cravings for unusual things are signs of early pregnancy. Maybe she’s pregnant?”

MC: “Pregnant? That’s a possibility, I guess. But why would she be so upset about it?”

Sayori: “Well, maybe she’s scared or unsure about what to do. I’ll try talking to her later and see if she opens up about it. In the meantime, let’s just give her some space and support.”

MC: “Yeah, good idea. Let’s make sure she knows we’re here for her if she needs us.”

(Later that day, Sayori and I check up on Natsuki.)

Natsuki: (tearfully) “I…I am pregnant. I don’t know what to do. I’m scared and I feel so alone.”

Sayori: “Natsuki, we’re here for you. You’re not alone in this. We’ll support you no matter what decision you make.”

MC: “Yeah, we care about you, Natsuki. Just know that we’re here to help and listen.”

Natsuki: (sniffling) “Thank you…thank you both. I don’t know what I would do without you guys.”

(Sayori and I embrace Natsuki, comforting her during this difficult time.)

MC: “We’re in this together, Natsuki. We’ll figure things out as a team.”

(Natsuki smiles through her tears, grateful for our support. On the day of the festival, Natsuki was in her 7th month of pregnancy. We made sure to take care of her, making sure she was comfortable and had everything she needed. But just as I was putting the booth together, I hear Natsuki gasp in pain.)

Natsuki: (clutching her stomach) “Oh no…it’s happening! My water just broke!”

MC: (panicking) “What?! But Natsuki, you’re only in your 7th month! Try to hold on a bit longer!”

Natsuki: “I-I-I don’t think I can! The contractions are getting stronger!”

(Sayori quickly calls an ambulance as I hold Natsuki’s hand and try to reassure her. I start timing her contractions as we wait for the ambulance to arrive.)

MC: “Hang in there, Natsuki. You’re strong and brave. You can do this.”

Natsuki: (gritting her teeth) “I-I’ll try, MC. Just…just stay with me. It hurts so much…”

(The ambulance finally arrives after hours, but Natsuki was already in active labor by then.)

Good luck with your THWAY memecoin project! With the right strategy and execution, you can capitalize on the PEPE hype and create a successful memecoin of your own.

input.task:
(In the school literature clubroom…)

MC (me): “Natsuki, what’s wrong? You seem…angry. Well, you’re always angry, but today you’re especially angry.”

Natsuki: “MC, that’s none of your business! Just leave me alone. I don’t need your sympathy or anyone else’s for that matter.”

(I watch as Natsuki quickly packs up her things and storms out of the room, slamming the door behind her.)

MC: (sighing) “I hope she’s okay…I’ll have to check on her later.”

(Sayori approaches me, concern written all over her face.)

Sayori: “MC, do you think there’s something wrong with Natsuki?”

MC: “Probably, Sayori. She’s been acting a lot angrier than normal lately. What do you think is wrong with her?”

Sayori: “Well, I also saw her eating pickles and brocolli with her cupcakes - which she normally wouldn’t do, considering she’s got a sweet tooth. I actually read that mood swings and cravings for unusual things are signs of early pregnancy. Maybe she’s pregnant?”

MC: “Pregnant? That’s a possibility, I guess. But why would she be so upset about it?”

Sayori: “Well, maybe she’s scared or unsure about what to do. I’ll try talking to her later and see if she opens up about it. In the meantime, let’s just give her some space and support.”

MC: “Yeah, good idea. Let’s make sure she knows we’re here for her if she needs us.”

(Later that day, Sayori and I check up on Natsuki.)

Natsuki: (tearfully) “I…I am pregnant. I don’t know what to do. I’m scared and I feel so alone.”

Sayori: “Natsuki, we’re here for you. You’re not alone in this. We’ll support you no matter what decision you make.”

MC: “Yeah, we care about you, Natsuki. Just know that we’re here to help and listen.”

Natsuki: (sniffling) “Thank you…thank you both. I don’t know what I would do without you guys.”

(Sayori and I embrace Natsuki, comforting her during this difficult time.)

MC: “We’re in this together, Natsuki. We’ll figure things out as a team.”

(Natsuki smiles through her tears, grateful for our support. On the day of the festival, Natsuki was in her 7th month of pregnancy. We made sure to take care of her, making sure she was comfortable and had everything she needed. But just as I was putting the booth together, I hear Natsuki gasp in pain.)

Natsuki: (clutching her stomach) “Oh no…it’s happening! My water just broke!”

MC: (panicking) “What?! But Natsuki, you’re only in your 7th month! Try to hold on a bit longer!”

Natsuki: “I-I-I don’t think I can! The contractions are getting stronger!”

(Sayori quickly calls an ambulance as I hold Natsuki’s hand and try to reassure her. I start timing her contractions as we wait for the ambulance to arrive.)

MC: “Hang in there, Natsuki. You’re strong and brave. You can do this.”

Natsuki: (gritting her teeth) “I-I’ll try, MC. Just…just stay with me. It hurts so much…”

(The ambulance finally arrives after hours, but Natsuki was already in active labor by then.)

input.response:
(As the paramedics rush to Natsuki's side, I help them lift her onto the stretcher, trying to remain calm and supportive. Sayori and I exchange worried glances, but we know we have to be strong for Natsuki. We follow the ambulance to the hospital, holding hands and praying for Natsuki and her baby's safety.

At the hospital, we wait anxiously in the lobby, pacing back and forth and trying to distract ourselves with small talk. After what feels like an eternity, a doctor approaches us with a serious expression. Our hearts sink, fearing the worst. However, the doctor's words bring a wave of relief.)

Doctor: "Natsuki and her baby are stable now. She gave birth to a healthy but premature baby girl. They're both in the NICU for observation and care. Natsuki is exhausted but doing well, considering the circumstances. You can see her soon, but only for a short while, as she needs her rest."

(Sayori and I share a tearful hug, grateful for the good news. We're led to Natsuki's room, where we find her looking tired but radiant, holding her tiny baby girl in her arms. Natsuki smiles weakly at us, and we approach her bedside, our hearts filled with love and admiration for her strength.)

Natsuki: (whispering) "Meet my little girl, Hana. She's so small, but she's a fighter, just like her mom."

MC: (teary-eyed) "She's beautiful, Natsuki. You did an amazing job. We're so proud of you."

Sayori: (gently touching Hana's tiny hand) "We'll be here for you both, every step of the way. You're not alone, Natsuki."

(In the following weeks, we help Natsuki adjust to her new role as a mother, taking turns visiting her and Hana at the hospital and supporting her in any way we can. When Hana is finally strong enough to go home, we celebrate with a small, intimate party at the literature clubroom, welcoming the newest member of our little family.)

(As I watch Natsuki cradle Hana, I can't help but feel a sense of awe and gratitude for the incredible journey we've all been through together. Our bond as friends has only grown stronger, and I know that, no matter what challenges we may face in the future, we'll always be there for each other, just like we were for Natsuki and Hana.)
